# Roadmap: SEC filing-index ingestion

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

Order follows dependency, not the O1–O11 ranking: the core stage proves the
quarterly baseline on real data first; manifest, replay and publication come
before daily ingestion because daily catch-up tracks pending sources in the
manifest; Azure and the shared lease come after the behaviors they host; the
configuration contract and scheduled operation close the track.

- [ ] Stage 1: Local quarterly baseline
      Objective: Discover, download and keep a configured inclusive range of real archived quarterly master indexes through one throttled, identified downloader, and parse them into canonical rows in Parquet on a local machine.
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: nothing; the four packages are `uv init` scaffolds.
      Produces: a `sec-edgar-ingest` CLI with quarterly discover, collect and transform; content-addressed raw snapshots; `sec-index-v1` row Parquet; golden fixtures for the formats in the run's range; the local storage layout later stages build on; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md.
      Exit: O1 — every quarter in the requested real range has its original bytes stored under its SHA-256, or is reported failed or quarantined; O3 — those quarters' rows are in Parquet meeting the §4.5 row contract, with malformed rows refused and reported, not dropped; cost — the findings file records bytes, row counts, elapsed time, peak memory, request count and observed request rate of the real run.
      Leaves out: source manifest, worksets, versioned generations, active pointer and replay → Stage 2; daily sources → Stage 3; reconciliation and the withdrawal gate → Stage 4; Azure services and the Storage-lease request budget → Stage 5; typed configuration validation, schedules, alerts, runbooks and the full §6 suite → Stage 6.
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Manifest, replay and quarter publication
      Objective: Record source, snapshot, processing and attempt state, rebuild from stored bytes, and publish each quarter as an immutable generation behind a conditional active pointer.
      Outcomes: O6, O9
      Consumes: Stage 1 raw snapshots, row Parquet, CLI and storage layout (plan <id>, Handoff).
      Produces: the §4.5 manifest records on a local stand-in for Table Storage; immutable worksets; observation output keyed by snapshot, parser and schema; quarter generations with manifest.json and changes.parquet; a `publish` command and reader pointer resolution.
      Exit: O6 — a parser-version bump rebuilds Stage 1's quarters from stored bytes with zero SEC requests and the same logical catalog; O9 — a reader following each quarter's pointer gets exactly the manifest's file list, and a crash injected before the pointer update leaves the previous generation readable.
      Leaves out: ADLS and Table Storage backing → Stage 5; withdrawal gate → Stage 4; the full §6 crash-injection and competing-publisher suite → Stage 6.
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Daily ingestion and catch-up
      Objective: Discover and ingest daily and quarter-to-date indexes from a handoff date, catching up after missed runs and revisiting pending sources, through the shared collect, transform and publish code.
      Outcomes: O2, O5
      Consumes: Stage 2 manifest, worksets and publish (plan <id>, Handoff).
      Produces: daily discovery with a durable discovery boundary; open-quarter precedence; the §4.7 run report counts and gaps.
      Exit: O2 — a real catch-up from a handoff date ingests every listed daily index across a quarter boundary and reports pending, failed and `no_new_sources` separately; O5 — backfill and daily runs execute the same collect, transform and publish commands, differing only in discovery's source selection.
      Leaves out: the shared Storage-lease budget → Stage 5; ADF daily schedule → Stage 6.
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: Reconciliation and withdrawal gate
      Objective: Re-read supported quarterly indexes, publish safe changes, and hold any closed-quarter candidate that removes keys until a hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stage 2 generations and change reports; Stage 3 open-quarter precedence (plan <id>, Handoff).
      Produces: reconciliation source selection; `awaiting_approval` candidates; withdrawal approval records; stale-daily resurrection guard.
      Exit: O7 — a reconciliation run over published quarters records additions and field updates in changes.parquet and skips unchanged hashes; O10 — a corrected closed-quarter fixture that removes keys stays `awaiting_approval` until an approval naming its hash and candidate generation, and a 404, empty response or open-quarter absence withdraws nothing.
      Leaves out: weekly schedule → Stage 6; approval records on Table Storage → Stage 5.
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Azure platform and shared request budget
      Objective: Run the shared image's commands as Container Apps Jobs under ADF in an isolated Azure environment on ADLS and Table Storage, with every collector under one Storage-backed lease.
      Outcomes: O4, O8
      Consumes: Stages 1–4 commands and storage contracts (plan <id>, Handoff).
      Produces: versioned infrastructure under infra/azure/sec-edgar-ingest/; managed identities; ADF pipelines with start/poll and worker-result checks; Storage-backed collector lease; structured logs in Log Analytics; production triggers disabled.
      Exit: O4 — in the isolated environment, ADF runs backfill, daily and reconciliation as Container Apps Jobs writing to ADLS and Table Storage, logs reach Log Analytics, and an ambiguous start launches no second copy; O8 — concurrent backfill, daily and reconciliation collectors together never exceed the configured rate, with retries counted and lease loss stopping requests.
      Leaves out: schedules and trigger enablement, alerts, runbooks and the release record → Stage 6.
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Configuration contract and scheduled operation
      Objective: Enforce the §4.8 configuration contract, complete the §6 suite, and take the system through §7 Phase 2 to observed scheduled operation.
      Outcomes: O11
      Consumes: Stage 5 deployed environment (plan <id>, Handoff).
      Produces: typed conf/sec-edgar-ingest.yaml validated before network I/O; ADF Eastern-time schedules; §4.7 alerts; §8 runbooks; the full §6 CI exit criteria; the release record of image digest, configuration revision and active generations.
      Exit: O11 — every §4.8 key validates before any request, an invalid configuration (a rate at or above the ceiling, a second collector, a missing identity) is refused before I/O, and the first scheduled daily and reconciliation runs are observed against their durable reports with the stated defaults in force.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans
